mainTopic: אין שליח לדבר עבירה (its source and שמאי's view on a sender to murder), and whether a שליח can also be an עד
overview: The גמרא asks why we don't learn from מעילה and from a thief's טביחה ומכירה that a sender is responsible for a sin his שליח commits. It answers that these are שני כתובים הבאים כאחד, two verses that teach the same idea, and such verses cannot be a model for other cases. According to the opinion that two such verses do teach, the תורה says "that man" twice about שחוטי חוץ, and the extra word spreads the rule אין שליח לדבר עבירה to the whole תורה. The גמרא then explains how each opinion reads the words "הוא" and "ההוא". Next comes a ברייתא in which שמאי הזקן says a man who sends someone to kill is liable, based on the פסוק about דוד and אוריה. The גמרא gives three ways to explain שמאי. רבא adds that even שמאי agrees the sender is exempt for sins of pleasure like ערוה and חלב. Finally, רב and דבי רבי שילא argue whether a שליח can also be an עד, and the הלכה is that he can. So two agents sent for קידושין or גירושין also serve as the witnesses, and that statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not learn a general rule from the exceptions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes learning from מעילה that a שליח can act for a sender even when the act is a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule of אין שליח לדבר עבירה. Since we already know that in מעילה the sender is liable for his agent's act, why not apply that everywhere?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא showed that in מעילה the sender is responsible for what his שליח did. The challenge says this case should become the model for the whole תורה. If it did, the rule אין שליח לדבר עבירה would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing הקדש (holy property) for personal benefit

phrases.english: Let us learn from it!
phrases.notes: "It" is מעילה, where we already saw that the sender is liable for what his agent did.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the earlier discussion of מעילה as a case where the agency of a שליח works for a sin.
steps.kashyaTarget: The general rule אין שליח לדבר עבירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If מעילה shows that a שליח can act for a sin, that case should become a model for all of the תורה.

steps.title: Two verses that teach the same idea cannot be a model
steps.stepSummary: We cannot learn from מעילה because it and טביחה ומכירה are שני כתובים הבאים כאחד, and such verses do not teach other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because מעילה and slaughtering and selling are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Since two separate verses teach this same exception, we cannot learn a general rule from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is this: if the idea applied to the whole תורה, the תורה would only need to write it once. Writing it twice, in מעילה and in טביחה ומכירה, shows the idea is limited to those cases. So they stay as exceptions and do not become the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering and selling a stolen animal, which makes a thief pay four or five times its value
Two verses that teach the same new idea
They do not teach, meaning other cases cannot be learned from them

steps.confusionAlert: Having two sources does not make the idea stronger here. The extra source shows the idea is limited, so it cannot spread to other cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle explains why the exceptions of מעילה and טביחה ומכירה do not cancel the general rule אין שליח לדבר עבירה.

phrases.english: Because מעילה
and slaughtering and selling
are two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה מְעִילָה טְבִיחָה וּמְכִירָה שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the source using an interpretive principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מעילה could be a model for all sins done through a שליח.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעילה and טביחה ומכירה are two verses with the same idea, so they stay as exceptions only.

steps.title: Where is the verse for slaughtering and selling?
steps.stepSummary: The verse for מעילה was already cited, so the גמרא asks for the verse showing a thief is liable when his agent slaughters or sells.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse for מעילה is the one we already said. What is the verse for slaughtering and selling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to clarify the answer it just gave. It already knows the source for מעילה, but it wants the source for the second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 2 only works if there really are two verses. So the גמרא checks that טביחה ומכירה has its own verse showing that a שליח counts.

phrases.english: מעילה is what we already said,
slaughtering and selling, what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the second of the two verses mentioned in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse showing that a thief is liable for slaughter or sale done by his שליח.

steps.title: Slaughter is compared to sale
steps.stepSummary: The verse puts slaughtering next to selling. Selling always involves another person, so slaughtering through another person also makes the thief liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And he slaughters it or sells it." Just as selling is done through another person, so too slaughtering can be done through another person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the second case. It learns it from the verse that links slaughtering with selling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sale always needs a buyer, so it always involves someone else. Because the תורה puts slaughtering in the same phrase, slaughtering also counts even when someone else does it for the thief. So the thief pays the penalty even if his שליח did the slaughtering.

keyTerms.meaning: And he slaughters it or sells it

phrases.english: The verse says: "And he slaughters it or sells it"
phrases.notes: שמות 21:37

phrases.english: just as selling is through another person,
so too slaughtering can be through another person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Placing slaughtering next to selling in the verse teaches that slaughter through a שליח also makes the thief liable.

steps.title: דבי רבי ישמעאל: the word "or" includes an agent
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns the liability for a שליח from the word "או" in the same verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: "Or" comes to include the agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second way to find the same source. This one uses the single word "או" (or) in the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have said "slaughters it, sells it" without "or." The school of רבי ישמעאל reads the extra word as adding the case of a שליח. The result is the same, but the source is different.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught

phrases.english: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
"Or" comes to include the agent.
phrases.notes: This is the "or" in "he slaughters it or sells it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same law answered in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word "או" adds the case of a שליח to the thief's penalty.

steps.title: דבי חזקיה: the word "in place of" includes an agent
steps.stepSummary: The school of חזקיה learns the liability for a שליח from the word "תחת" in the verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of חזקיה taught: "In place of" comes to include the agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third source for the same idea. This one uses the word "תחת" in the verse about the penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says "five cattle in place of the ox, and four sheep in place of the sheep." Repeating "תחת" is not needed, so the school of חזקיה uses it to add the case of a שליח.

phrases.english: The school of חזקיה taught:
"In place of" comes to include the agent.
phrases.notes: From the same verse: "five cattle in place of the ox, and four sheep in place of the sheep."

steps.whatToRemember: All three sources agree that a thief is liable for slaughter or sale done by his שליח. This is the second of the "two verses" alongside מעילה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative source, parallel to step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra word "תחת" adds the case of a שליח to the thief's penalty.

steps.title: What about the opinion that two verses do teach?
steps.stepSummary: The answer from step 2 only works for one opinion. According to the view that שני כתובים הבאים כאחד do teach, why don't we learn from מעילה and טביחה ומכירה?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says two verses that come as one do not teach. But for the one who says they do teach, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. Some תנאים hold that two such verses can teach other cases, so for them the problem from step 1 comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 depended on the rule that two verses teaching the same idea cannot spread. There is a dispute about that rule. According to the view that they can teach, מעילה and טביחה ומכירה should make a general rule that a שליח counts for a sin.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for the one who says

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד אֵין מְלַמְּדִין.
phrases.english: two verses that come as one do not teach.
But for the one who says they do teach,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד אֵין מְלַמְּדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the answer of step 2 and shows it does not work for every opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 2, which relies on שני כתובים הבאים כאחד אין מלמדין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For the opinion that two such verses do teach, the exceptions should become a general rule, and the challenge of step 1 returns.

steps.title: שחוטי חוץ shows the sender is not liable
steps.stepSummary: The תורה says about slaughtering a קרבן outside the Temple, "that man," which teaches that only he is liable and not someone who sent him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Merciful One revealed in שחוטי חוץ: "It shall be counted as blood for that man; he has spilled blood." He, and not his agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the second opinion. The תורה itself shows in one case that a sender is not responsible for his שליח's sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "ההוא" (that man) points only to the person who actually did the slaughtering, not to someone who sent him. So in שחוטי חוץ, at least, the תורה openly says the sender is not liable. The next steps ask how this one case can become the rule for the whole תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering a קרבן outside the Temple

phrases.english: The Merciful One revealed about slaughtering outside:
"It shall be counted as blood for that man;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4

phrases.english: he has spilled blood"
he, and not his agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an explicit verse that teaches the opposite rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to the opinion that two verses do teach, a שליח would count for every sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה openly says in שחוטי חוץ that the sender is not liable. Steps 9–12 show how this spreads to the whole תורה.

steps.title: How do we know this for the whole תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The verse speaks only about שחוטי חוץ. Where do we learn that the rule applies to every sin in the תורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found this about שחוטי חוץ. From where do we know it for the whole תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how far the verse reaches. The verse only spoke about slaughtering outside the Temple.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A verse about one sin might be limited to that sin. The גמרא needs a reason to spread "he, and not his agent" to all other sins.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: We have found it regarding slaughtering outside;
for the whole תורה, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן גַּבֵּי שְׁחוּטֵי חוּץ, בְּכׇל הַתּוֹרָה מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how widely the source from step 8 applies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that spreads the rule "he, and not his agent" from שחוטי חוץ to all sins.

steps.title: The whole תורה learns from שחוטי חוץ
steps.stepSummary: All other sins learn from שחוטי חוץ that there is no שליח for a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from שחוטי חוץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שחוטי חוץ is the model for the whole תורה. So the rule אין שליח לדבר עבירה applies everywhere except the special exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here שחוטי חוץ is one single case and not two verses teaching the same idea, so even the stricter rule lets other cases learn from it. The general rule therefore comes from שחוטי חוץ. מעילה and טביחה ומכירה remain special exceptions.

phrases.english: It is learned from slaughtering outside.

steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to keep the rule אין שליח לדבר עבירה. (1) מעילה and טביחה ומכירה are two verses teaching the same idea, so they don't spread. (2) Even for the opinion that they do teach, the תורה openly says "he, and not his agent" in שחוטי חוץ, and the whole תורה learns from that.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The whole תורה learns from שחוטי חוץ that a sender is not liable for his agent's sin.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אין שליח לדבר עבירה applies throughout the תורה, learned from שחוטי חוץ. מעילה and טביחה ומכירה are exceptions.

steps.title: Why learn from slaughtering outside and not from the other cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why all sins should follow שחוטי חוץ rather than מעילה and טביחה ומכירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Instead of learning from שחוטי חוץ, let us learn from those other cases!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 10, which said all sins learn from שחוטי חוץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of cases. In שחוטי חוץ the sender is not liable, but in מעילה and טביחה ומכירה he is. So why should the rest of the תורה follow the first case and not the second?

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering a קרבן outside the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Before learning from slaughtering outside,
phrases.notes: "Those" in the next line means מעילה and טביחה ומכירה, where a שליח does make the sender liable.

phrases.english: let us learn from those!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that all sins learn from שחוטי חוץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are opposite cases (מעילה, טביחה ומכירה) that could serve as the model just as well

steps.title: The extra word teaches the rule for the whole תורה
steps.stepSummary: The second "ההוא" in the פסוק is not needed for שחוטי חוץ itself, so it teaches the rule for the whole תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה writes again: "And that man shall be cut off." If this is not needed for its own case, apply it to the whole תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a second "ההוא" in the same פסוק tells us to apply the rule everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first "לאיש ההוא" already taught that there is no שליח in שחוטי חוץ. The second one is extra, so we use it as a teaching for every sin. This beats learning from מעילה and טביחה ומכירה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for its own topic

steps.whatToRemember: The extra "ההוא" in שחוטי חוץ is what makes אין שליח לדבר עבירה a rule for the entire תורה.

phrases.english: The Merciful One wrote again:
"And that man shall be cut off" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:4

phrases.english: if it is not needed for its own matter,
apply it to the matter of the entire Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק teaches a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might learn the rule for all sins from מעילה and טביחה ומכירה
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra "ההוא" applies אין שליח לדבר עבירה to the whole תורה

steps.title: What does the other view learn from the two words
steps.stepSummary: The view that שני כתובים הבאים כאחד do not teach has nothing to block, so it does not need either "ההוא" for the rule about a שליח. What does it learn from these words?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says two verses that come as one do not teach, what does he learn from these two "that" words?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the two "ההוא" words teach for the view that does not need them to answer מעילה and טביחה ומכירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For this view, מעילה and טביחה ומכירה could never teach a general rule anyway. So he does not need an extra word to block them. The גמרא wants to know what these words teach for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses teaching the same thing
What does he learn from them?

phrases.english: And according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד אֵין מְלַמְּדִים,
phrases.english: two verses that come as one do not teach,
these words "that" and "that"
phrases.notes: These are the two times ויקרא 17:4 says "that man" about slaughtering outside.

phrases.english: what does he learn from them?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד אֵין מְלַמְּדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the other view after step 12 answered the first view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the two "ההוא" words teach for the view that rejects שני כתובים הבאים כאחד

steps.title: Two people slaughtering together, and someone forced or mistaken
steps.stepSummary: One "ההוא" leaves out two people who slaughter together. The other leaves out someone forced, someone who acted by accident, and someone who was misled.
steps.simpleTranslation: One teaches that two who hold a knife and slaughter are not liable. The other teaches "he" and not one who was forced, "he" and not one who acted by accident, "he" and not one who was misled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this view uses the two words for other laws about שחוטי חוץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "That man" means one single person acting fully on purpose. So two people slaughtering together are not liable. Someone who was אנוס, שוגג, or מוטעה is not liable either.

keyTerms.meaning: Misled or mistaken about the facts

phrases.english: One is to leave out two people
who hold a knife and slaughter together,
and one: "he", and not one who was forced,
"he", and not one who acted by accident,
"he", and not one who was misled.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד, לְמַעוֹטֵי שְׁנַיִם שֶׁאוֹחֲזִים בְּסַכִּין וְשׁוֹחֲטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One "ההוא" leaves out two people slaughtering together; the other leaves out אנוס, שוגג and מוטעה

steps.title: Where does the first view learn these laws
steps.stepSummary: The view that accepts שני כתובים הבאים כאחד used the words for שליחות, so where does it learn these laws?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the first view learns the laws of step 14, since it already used both words for the rule about a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view used both "ההוא" words for אין שליח לדבר עבירה. So no word seems left over for the laws about two slaughterers and someone forced or mistaken.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other view)?

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: He means the view that does accept שני כתובים הבאים כאחד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the first view to explain where it learns the laws of step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the laws of step 14 according to the view that used "ההוא" for שליחות

steps.title: He learns from both parts of the word
steps.stepSummary: He learns separate laws from "הוא" and from the added ה in "ההוא".
steps.simpleTranslation: From "he" and from "that".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first view splits the word "ההוא" into parts and learns from each part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "הוא" alone would have been enough. The extra ה gives one more teaching. So this view has enough room for both the שליח rule and the laws of step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (הוא with an extra ה)

phrases.english: From "he" and "that".
phrases.notes: The פסוק could have said just "הוא". It says "ההוא", so the extra letter is used for another teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learns extra laws from the difference between "הוא" and "ההוא"

steps.title: Why the second view does not do the same
steps.stepSummary: Why doesn't the second view also split the word and learn more?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the view that rejects שני כתובים הבאים כאחד does not also learn from the extra ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second view also split the word, it would have spare words left over. The גמרא asks why it does not read it that way.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Now he means the view that does not accept שני כתובים הבאים כאחד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the method of step 16 is not used by the second view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the second view does not learn from the difference between "הוא" and "ההוא"

steps.title: He does not learn from the extra letter
steps.stepSummary: The second view does not learn anything from the difference between "הוא" and "ההוא".
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not learn from "he" versus "that".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second view treats "ההוא" as one word and does not split it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For this view, each "ההוא" gives only one teaching. So the two words are used for the laws of step 14 and nothing more. The two views differ in how closely they read the word.
steps.whatToRemember: Both views learn the same laws. The difference is whether we learn from the extra ה in "ההוא", which gives the first view room to also learn אין שליח לדבר עבירה.

phrases.english: He does not learn from "he" versus "that".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second view does not split "ההוא" into parts

steps.title: A teaching about sending someone to kill
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a sender to murder is פטור. But שמאי הזקן, quoting חגי הנביא, says the sender is חייב. That goes against אין שליח לדבר עבירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: one who tells his agent "Go kill a person", the agent is liable and the sender is exempt. שמאי הזקן says in the name of חגי הנביא: the sender is liable, as it says, "Him you have killed with the sword of the children of עמון."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with an opinion that seems to say a person is responsible for a sin done through a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion fits the rule: only the killer is liable. But שמאי הזקן holds the sender liable, based on a פסוק. That seems to show there is a שליח for a sin, against everything the סוגיא has built so far.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is what was taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: The first opinion in the ברייתא agrees with the rule. Only שמאי הזקן's opinion causes the problem.

phrases.english: But there is what was taught:
One who says to his agent:
"Go kill a person,"
he (the agent) is liable, and the one who sent him is exempt.
Shammai the Elder says
in the name of Haggai the prophet:
the one who sent him is liable, as it is said:
"Him you have killed with the sword of the children of Ammon."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 12:9. נתן הנביא says this to דוד about אוריה, who was killed in battle through יואב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּתָנֵי: הָאוֹמֵר לִשְׁלוּחוֹ: ״צֵא הֲרוֹג אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about "ההוא" and challenges the main rule itself
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule אין שליח לדבר עבירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמאי הזקן holds the sender liable for murder done by his שליח, so it seems there is שליחות for a sin

steps.title: What is שמאי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind שמאי הזקן's ruling that the sender is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of שמאי הזקן?
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the challenge in step 19, the גמרא asks how שמאי הזקן can make the sender חייב. This question sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned that אין שליח לדבר עבירה, which means the sender should be פטור. שמאי says he is חייב, so the גמרא needs to find a logic that explains his view.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Shammai the Elder?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge in step 19 by asking for שמאי's reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis for שמאי's ruling that the sender is חייב, even though אין שליח לדבר עבירה.

steps.title: שמאי learns from the two verses and does not use הוא/ההוא
steps.stepSummary: שמאי holds that שני כתובים הבאים כאחד do teach a rule, so there is שליחות for a sin. He does not learn anything from 'הוא' vs. 'ההוא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that two verses that come as one do teach. And he does not learn anything from 'הוא' vs. 'ההוא'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמאי simply takes the other side of the earlier debate about learning from two verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the two cases of מעילה and טביחה ומכירה pointed toward שליחות working even for a sin. The only thing blocking that was the rule that two such verses do not teach, together with the דרשה from 'הוא'/'ההוא'. שמאי rejects both, so for him a sender to sin is responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses that teach the same rule; there is a debate whether a general rule can be learned from them

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד מְלַמְּדִין,
phrases.english: He holds: two verses that come as one do teach,
phrases.notes: These are the cases of מעילה and of טביחה ומכירה, where the sender is responsible for what the messenger did.

phrases.english: and he does not expound "hu" and "hahu."
phrases.notes: This is the דרשה from steps 16–18 about the extra ה in the פסוק about שחוטי חוץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד מְלַמְּדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמאי accepts שני כתובים הבאים כאחד מלמדין and rejects the הוא/ההוא דרשה, so he holds there is שליחות for a sin.

steps.title: שמאי means liable only by Heaven's laws
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: שמאי does accept the drasha, so a sender is not legally responsible. 'חייב' only means he is liable בדיני שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: really he does expound it. What does 'liable' mean? Liable in the laws of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to understand שמאי. He agrees there is no agent for a sin, and 'חייב' refers only to punishment from Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this answer שמאי does not argue on אין שליח לדבר עבירה at all. A human court cannot punish the sender. But שמאי says Heaven still holds him accountable.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
The laws of Heaven: punishment from ה׳, not from a בית דין

steps.confusionAlert: 'חייב בדיני שמים' does not mean the court punishes him. It means a human court is powerless here and only Heaven judges him.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: actually he does expound it,
and what does "liable" mean? Liable in the laws of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמאי's 'חייב' means real legal liability, against אין שליח לדבר עבירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חייב' means only בדיני שמים, so שמאי agrees with אין שליח לדבר עבירה.

steps.title: Would the תנא קמא say he is fully exempt even from Heaven?
steps.stepSummary: If שמאי's point is only Heavenly liability, then the תנא קמא must hold the sender is free even from Heaven. That is hard to accept.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that imply the first תנא holds he is exempt even from the laws of Heaven?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second answer. If שמאי is arguing, the תנא קמא must say the sender is fully exempt even before Heaven, and that seems impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every argument needs two sides. If שמאי adds 'liable בדיני שמים', the other side would be 'not liable even in Heaven'. It is very hard to say that a person who arranged a murder carries no guilt at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: By implication, the first Tanna holds:
he is exempt even from the laws of Heaven?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שמאי means חייב בדיני שמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that is the argument, the תנא קמא must hold the sender has no guilt even before Heaven, which is unreasonable.

steps.title: A big judgment versus a small judgment
steps.stepSummary: Both agree the sender is liable בדיני שמים. They argue only about how severe the Heavenly judgment is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: a big judgment and a small judgment is the difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. Both sides hold the sender is punished by Heaven; they argue about how much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי holds the Heavenly judgment is severe, as if the sender did it himself. The תנא קמא holds the sender is guilty only to a smaller degree. So nobody says he is totally free of guilt.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: דִּינָא רַבָּה וְדִינָא זוּטָא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: Rather: a great judgment and a small judgment is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: דִּינָא רַבָּה וְדִינָא זוּטָא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the argument to a difference in degree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא exempts the sender even from Heaven.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree there is Heavenly liability; they argue only about whether it is severe or light.

steps.title: Murder is different because the verse says so
steps.stepSummary: A third answer: in general there is no agent for a sin, but murder is different because the פסוק blames דוד for killing אוריה by the sword of בני עמון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: there it is different, because the תורה revealed: 'Him you killed with the sword of בני עמון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more way to explain שמאי. Everyone holds אין שליח לדבר עבירה, but murder is a special exception taught by a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד did not kill אוריה with his own hands; he had it done in battle. Yet the נביא tells him 'you killed him'. שמאי learns from this that in murder the one who arranges it is held responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: The Ammonites, the enemy army in the battle where אוריה died

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps the general rule of אין שליח לדבר עבירה. It only makes murder a special case, an exception learned from a פסוק.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: there it is different,

phrases.aramaic: דְּגַלִּי רַחֲמָנָא: ״אֹתוֹ הָרַגְתָּ בְּחֶרֶב בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן״.
phrases.english: since the Merciful One revealed: "Him you have slain with the sword of the children of Ammon."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 12:9. נתן הנביא is speaking to דוד about אוריה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמאי argues on the general rule of אין שליח לדבר עבירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמאי agrees with the general rule; murder is an exception because of the פסוק about דוד and אוריה.

steps.title: How the other view reads the verse
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא reads the פסוק the opposite way: אוריה's death is like a death by the Ammonite sword in war, so דוד is not punished for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other view: it is for you like the sword of בני עמון. Just as you are not punished for the sword of בני עמון, so too you are not punished for אוריה החתי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the תנא קמא handles the same פסוק. He reads it as a comparison that frees דוד from punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמאי the words say 'you killed him'. The תנא קמא reads 'like the sword of בני עמון'. Deaths in battle by the enemy are not counted against the king, so אוריה's death is not counted against דוד either.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other opinion (how does he deal with this?)
Uriah the Hittite, בת שבע's husband, who died in battle at דוד's order

phrases.aramaic: וְאִידַּךְ: הֲרֵי לְךָ כְּחֶרֶב בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן,
phrases.english: And the other: behold, it is for you like the sword of the children of Ammon,

phrases.aramaic: מָה חֶרֶב בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן – אֵין אַתָּה נֶעֱנָשׁ עָלָיו,
phrases.english: just as for the sword of the children of Ammon you are not punished,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אוּרִיָּה הַחִתִּי – אִי אַתָּה נֶעֱנָשׁ עָלָיו.
phrases.english: so too for Uriah the Hittite you are not punished.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: הֲרֵי לְךָ כְּחֶרֶב בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the opposing view handles the פסוק used in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא reads the פסוק as a comparison: אוריה's death is like a battle death, and דוד is not punished for it.

steps.title: Uriah was a rebel against the king
steps.stepSummary: דוד was not punished because אוריה was a מורד במלכות. He called יואב 'my lord' in front of the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? He was a rebel against the kingdom, since he said to him: 'And my lord יואב and the servants of my lord are camped in the open field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אוריה's death did not count against דוד. אוריה had rebelled against the king and deserved death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Speaking to King דוד, אוריה called יואב 'my lord'. That treats someone else as master in front of the king, which counts as rebelling against the kingdom. So killing him was not punishable murder, and the תנא קמא does not need the פסוק as an exception to אין שליח לדבר עבירה.

keyTerms.meaning: A rebel against the king, who is liable to death

steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations of שמאי: (1) he learns from שני כתובים הבאים כאחד and rejects הוא/ההוא; (2) he means חייב בדיני שמים, a big vs. small judgment; (3) murder is different because of 'אותו הרגת'. The תנא קמא reads that פסוק as 'like the Ammonite sword', since אוריה was a מורד במלכות.

phrases.english: What is the reason? He was a rebel against the monarchy,
as he said to him: "And my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord,
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 11:11. אוריה is speaking to דוד, and calls יואב 'my lord' right in front of the king.

phrases.english: are encamped in the open field."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the reading in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אוריה was a מורד במלכות for calling יואב 'my lord' before the king, so his death was not punished.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For the תנא קמא, the story of דוד and אוריה is not a source that a sender to murder is liable, because אוריה was a rebel.

steps.title: Even שמאי agrees about forbidden relations and forbidden fat
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even if שמאי holds a sender is liable for his agent's sin, he agrees that in cases of ערוה and חלב only the agent is liable, since only he enjoys the act.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even if you say שמאי learns from 'two verses that come as one' and does not draw any lesson from the difference between 'הוא' and 'ההוא', he still agrees that if someone tells his agent 'Go have relations with a forbidden relative' or 'Go eat forbidden fat', the agent is liable and the sender is exempt. We never find anywhere in the תורה that one person enjoys the sin and a different person is punished for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets a limit on שמאי's view that the sender is responsible for his agent's sin. Even שמאי admits there are cases where only the agent is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose שמאי really holds there is agency for a sin in every case, based on how he reads the פסוקים. Even so, sins like ערוה and eating חלב are different, because the act gives physical pleasure to the person doing it. The תורה never punishes one person when someone else got the enjoyment, so the sender is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (going with the strongest version of the other view)
One person enjoys the sin while another is punished. The תורה never does this.

steps.whatToRemember: Even by שמאי, agency for a sin cannot make the sender liable for sins of physical pleasure like ערוה and חלב, because the sender got no enjoyment from them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the long discussion of שליח לדבר עבירה. It shows that even the opinion that holds the sender liable has a firm limit.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If you say that Shammai holds
that two verses that come as one do teach,
and he does not expound 'hu' and 'hahu',
phrases.notes: He means שמאי learns nothing from the פסוק switching between the short word הוּא and the longer הַהוּא.

phrases.english: he agrees about one who says to his agent
'Go have relations with a forbidden relative'
or 'eat forbidden fat'
that he is liable and the one who sent him is exempt.
phrases.notes: The 'he' here is the agent, the one who actually did the act.

phrases.english: For we have not found in the entire Torah
that this one benefits and that one becomes liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא: אם תמצי לומר סבר שמאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the שמאי discussion by limiting his view, even at its strongest reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even by שמאי, in ערוה and חלב only the agent is liable, since the תורה never punishes one person for another person's pleasure.

steps.title: Can an agent also be a witness
steps.stepSummary: A new argument: רב says a שליח can serve as an עד, while דבי רבי שילא say he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב says an agent can become a witness. The school of רבי שילא says an agent cannot become a witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand new topic. It asks whether the person who carried out an act as a שליח can later testify that the act happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture someone sent to do קידושין for another man. Can he also be one of the two עדים who see the קידושין? רב says yes, and דבי רבי שילא say no.

keyTerms.meaning: An agent sent to act for someone else

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav says:
An agent can become a witness.
The school of Rabbi Sheila say:
An agent cannot become a witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: איתמר, רב אמר: שליח נעשה עד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, still about the laws of שליחות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a שליח can be an עד. דבי רבי שילא: he cannot.

steps.title: Why does the school of Rabbi Sheila disqualify the agent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind דבי רבי שילא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the school of רבי שילא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why דבי רבי שילא say an agent cannot be a witness. This question sets up the next move, where a possible reason will be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing obvious disqualifies an agent. He is not a relative and he gains nothing, so the גמרא needs to find the logic behind disqualifying him.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the school of Rabbi Sheila?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind one side of the dispute just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason an agent cannot also serve as a witness.

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that he was never appointed as a witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the agent is disqualified because he was never told to be a witness. It rejects this, because witnesses to קידושין never need to be formally appointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because the sender never told him 'Be a witness for me', then according to that, if a man betrothed a woman in front of two people and never told them 'You are my witnesses', would the betrothal also not be valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out a reason for דבי רבי שילא and knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested reason is that the sender appointed him only as a שליח, not as an עד. But we know that two people who simply watch קידושין are valid עדים even if nobody appointed them. So being formally appointed cannot be what matters.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
But if so, then... (introduces an unacceptable result)

phrases.english: If we say it is because he did not say to him:
'Be a witness for me',
then according to that,
if one betrothed a woman in front of two people
and did not say to them 'You are my witnesses',
would it also be that it is not a valid betrothal?

steps.triggerLanguage: אילימא משום דלא אמר ליה הוי לי עד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a possible answer to the question and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested reason that a שליח is disqualified because he was not appointed as an עד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Witnesses to קידושין are valid without being appointed, so lacking an appointment cannot disqualify anyone.

steps.title: רב's reason: the agent's testimony is stronger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the dispute in a new way. רב says the agent is a good witness, because his testimony is even stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב says an agent can become a witness, because we are only strengthening his words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts over with a new explanation of the dispute, beginning with רב's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רב, being the agent does not weaken a witness. It actually makes his testimony stronger, because he did the act himself and knows for sure that it happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. This drops the earlier suggestion and offers a new one.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav says:
an agent can become a witness,
because we are strengthening his words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא, רב אמר: שליח נעשה עד – אלומי קא מאלימנא למילתיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first reason failed, the גמרא gives a fresh explanation of the dispute, starting with רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the dispute with new reasoning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about whether the agent had been appointed as a witness.
steps.terutzMaskana: By רב, the agent's firsthand knowledge makes him an even stronger witness.

steps.title: רבי שילא's reason: the agent counts as the sender himself
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי שילא disqualify the agent because a שליח counts as the sender himself, and a person cannot testify about his own act.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי שילא says an agent cannot become a witness. Since the Master said 'A person's agent is like himself', the agent counts as the sender in person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason for דבי רבי שילא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule שלוחו של אדם כמותו means the agent stands in place of the sender. The sender obviously cannot be a witness for his own קידושין, so neither can the person standing in his place.

keyTerms.meaning: A person's agent is like himself
Like his own body, meaning like the sender in person

steps.confusionAlert: The agent is not disqualified because he is untrustworthy. He is disqualified because legally he counts as the person doing the act, and that person cannot testify about his own act.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Sheila say:
an agent cannot become a witness,
since the Master said:
'A person's agent is like himself',
he counts as the sender himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: דבי רבי שילא אמרי: אין שליח נעשה עד – כיון דאמר מר שלוחו של אדם כמותו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the new explanation by giving the other side's reasoning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because a שליח is legally the sender, he cannot testify about the sender's act.

steps.title: A ברייתא about sending three people to betroth a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב. בית שמאי say one of the three is the agent and two are witnesses. בית הלל say all three are agents, and an agent cannot be a witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: If someone told three people 'Go out and betroth the woman for me', one is an agent and two are witnesses. These are the words of בית שמאי. בית הלל say: They are all agents, and an agent cannot become a witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to use against רב. This is the setup, and the actual challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל say openly that a שליח cannot be an עד, which already sounds difficult for רב. The גמרא will point out that even בית שמאי seem to agree in a simpler case.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If one said to three people:
'Go out and betroth the woman for me',
one is an agent and two are witnesses;
these are the words of Beit Shammai.
And Beit Hillel say:
They are all agents,
and an agent cannot become a witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: מיתיבי: אמר לשלשה צאו וקדשו לי האשה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to challenge רב's view from the previous steps.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a שליח can become an עד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית הלל explicitly say a שליח cannot be an עד, and the inference in the next step will show that even בית שמאי agree in one case.

steps.title: With only two people, everyone agrees agents are not witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely: the argument is only about three people. If a man sends two, both are agents, and all agree they cannot be the witnesses. This contradicts רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree when he spoke to three. But when he spoke to two, everyone agrees they cannot be witnesses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge against רב by drawing a conclusion from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי allow two of the three to be עדים only because one extra person can serve as the agent. If only two were sent, both are agents, and even בית שמאי would not let them be עדים. So every opinion in the ברייתא holds that an agent cannot be a witness, which is hard for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue as far as this case

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי אֶלָּא בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה,
phrases.english: They disagree only about a case of three,
but with two, everyone agrees they cannot be witnesses!

steps.triggerLanguage: עד כאן לא פליגי אלא בשלשה, אבל בשנים דברי הכל לא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge by drawing a conclusion from the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a שליח can become an עד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since even בית שמאי agree that when two are sent they cannot be the witnesses, every opinion holds that a שליח cannot be an עד, against רב.

steps.title: רב follows the version of רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from the ברייתא. רב holds like a different תנא, רבי נתן, whose version says the agent plus only one more witness is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said his ruling following this תנא. As it is taught: רבי נתן says, בית שמאי say: the agent and one witness. And בית הלל say: the agent and two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by bringing a different ברייתא in which the agent himself can count as a witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא seemed to say everyone agrees an agent cannot be a witness. But רבי נתן reports the dispute differently. In his version, בית שמאי say the agent plus one other person is enough, so the agent counts as the second witness. That is רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from the time of the משנה and ברייתא

phrases.english: It is he who said it like this תנא,
phrases.notes: "He" is רב. He is relying on a different ברייתא than the one that challenged him.

phrases.english: As it is taught: רבי נתן says,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: שָׁלִיחַ וְעֵד אֶחָד.
phrases.english: בית שמאי say: the agent and one witness.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: שָׁלִיחַ וּשְׁנֵי עֵדִים.
phrases.english: And בית הלל say: the agent and two witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 35 by bringing another version of the dispute between the תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative tannaitic source: רב follows a different version of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא showed that everyone agrees an agent cannot be a witness, which goes against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי נתן's version, there is a תנא who holds that an agent can be a witness, and רב follows him.

steps.title: Would רב really follow בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: in רבי נתן's version, the view that the agent counts as a witness belongs to בית שמאי. Would רב really rule like בית שמאי?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רב hold like בית שמאי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the answer it just gave, because it makes רב side with בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is that we do not follow בית שמאי when they argue with בית הלל. So it is hard to believe that רב, a major אמורא, would build his ruling on בית שמאי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי, whose views are usually not followed against בית הלל
The school of הלל, whose views are normally the הלכה

phrases.english: And does רב hold like בית שמאי?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב follows רבי נתן's version of בית שמאי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה normally does not follow בית שמאי against בית הלל, so it is unlikely that רב would side with them.

steps.title: Reverse the opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by switching the names in רבי נתן's version, so that בית הלל are the ones who say the agent plus one witness is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by swapping who said what in רבי נתן's ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the swap, בית הלל say an agent can count as a witness. Now רב follows בית הלל, which is the normal way the הלכה goes.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it, meaning swap the opinions between the two sides

phrases.english: Reverse it.
phrases.notes: Switch the names in רבי נתן's version, so בית הלל say "the agent and one witness."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in Step 37.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the attributions in the source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב would be following בית שמאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: With the names reversed, רב follows בית הלל.

steps.title: רב אחא בריה דרבא reports the dispute the other way around
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא had a different version of the argument between the אמוראים. In his version, רב says an agent cannot be a witness, and דבי רבי שילא say he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אחא the son of רבא taught it the opposite way: רב said: An agent cannot become a witness. The school of רבי שילא say: An agent can become a witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another way to solve the problem: switch the opinions of the אמוראים instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב holds that an agent cannot be a witness. That fits the first ברייתא perfectly, so the challenge against רב disappears. Now it is דבי רבי שילא who hold that an agent can be a witness.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught, meaning he reported the statement
An agent can become a witness

steps.confusionAlert: Careful! In this version the names are flipped: רב is the one who disqualifies the agent, the opposite of what we learned before.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מַתְנִי אִיפְּכָא:
phrases.english: And רב אחא the son of רבא taught it the opposite way:

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: אֵין שָׁלִיחַ נַעֲשֶׂה עֵד,
phrases.english: רב said: An agent cannot become a witness,

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵי רַבִּי שֵׁילָא אָמְרִי: שָׁלִיחַ נַעֲשֶׂה עֵד.
phrases.english: The school of רבי שילא say: An agent can become a witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מַתְנִי אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another way to remove the challenge from Step 35: reverse the אמוראים instead of the תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different version of who said each opinion among the אמוראים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב says an agent can be a witness, which goes against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב actually says an agent cannot be a witness, which matches the ברייתא.

steps.title: The halacha: an agent can be a witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the final הלכה is that an agent can serve as a witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: An agent can become a witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion with a final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whichever version of the names is correct, the practical law is now settled. The person who carries out the קידושין can also be one of the witnesses to it.

keyTerms.meaning: And the law is, used for a final ruling

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: a שליח can also be an עד for the act he carries out.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is: An agent can become a witness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute discussed in the earlier steps.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An agent can also serve as a witness.

steps.title: Two agents are also the two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רב נחמן: if a man tells two people to go and do קידושין for him, those same two are both his agents and his witnesses. The same is true for גירושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: If a man said to two people, "Go and betroth the woman for me," they themselves are his agents and they themselves are his witnesses. And the same is true for divorce,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical ruling that follows from the הלכה that an agent can be a witness. The statement continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since an agent may be a witness, no extra people are needed. The two agents together do the קידושין and also serve as the two required witnesses. רב נחמן applies the same rule to delivering a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Go and betroth, the man's instruction to his agents

steps.whyThisMatters: This puts the הלכה into practice: two people can handle a קידושין or a גט by themselves, without bringing any more witnesses.

phrases.english: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִשְׁנַיִם: ״צְאוּ וְקַדְּשׁוּ לִי אֶת הָאִשָּׁה״ –
phrases.english: If one said to two people: "Go and betroth the woman for me" –

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן שְׁלוּחָיו, הֵן הֵן עֵדָיו.
phrases.english: they themselves are his agents, they themselves are his witnesses.
And the same is true for divorce,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the final הלכה from Step 40 to a practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two agents sent for קידושין or גירושין also serve as the two witnesses.
